concept: Jito bundle submission and transaction landing
summary: Source-anchored research for Jito bundle submission and transaction landing. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: FullSend is a separate, access-gated Jito product: a Solana JSON-RPC sendTransaction endpoint that forwards signed transactions straight to current and upcoming leaders through stake-weighted QoS. It does not simulate transactions or track confirmation. Solana Compass reports that Jito's BAM maintenance notice says validators, FullSend users and standard bundle senders need take no action for the Alpenglow transition. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

FullSend is a separate, access-form-gated Jito service: a Solana-compatible JSON-RPC sendTransaction at https://mainnet.hudson.jito.wtf with an api_key query parameter, direct-to-leader SWQOS delivery, validator blacklists for MEV protection (default and custom, both on by default), and a browser-safe sendTransactionWeb that authenticates by authorized fee-payer signer. It runs no simulation and tracks no confirmation. Jito's BAM changelog says FullSend users needed no action during the Alpenglow BAM maintenance window. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Jito tips and Solana priority fees are separate levers: the tip ranks the bundle in the Block Engine auction, the priority fee affects runtime scheduling. Tips do nothing when the leader is not Jito-Solana. For single transactions via Jito sendTransaction, Jito advises setting both a priority fee and a tip; Chainstack suggests a 70/30 split between them. (medium confidence)

The Block Engine sendTransaction path (https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf/api/v1/transactions) proxies Solana's sendTransaction to the validator with MEV protection on by default and always sets skip_preflight=true, so the RPC does not simulate the transaction first. The query parameter bundleOnly=true sends the transaction only as a single-transaction bundle, which gives revert protection. When the send was made as a bundle, the bundle ID comes back in the x-bundle-id response header. (medium confidence)

If transactions from your bundle show up on an explorer as individual failed transactions, suspect an uncled block. When a block built by a leader is not accepted by the supermajority, any party that received it can rebroadcast its transactions, and those go through the normal banking stage without bundle atomicity or revert protection. Jito's mitigations are pre- and post-account checks so a rebroadcast is harmless, minimizing leakage, and keeping the tip in the same transaction as the strategy. (high confidence)

Put the tip instruction in the same transaction as the strategy logic with post-transaction checks; if space is short, add slot and balance assertions to a separate tip transaction (Jito's advice). The defence has an Ethereum precedent: Flashbots told users to add a parent-hash check, require(blockhash(block.number - 1) == expectedParentHash), because transactions from an uncled block become visible and targetable ('uncle bandit'); it cited roughly 1 in 20 Ethereum blocks being uncled at the time and the page is marked outdated. (medium confidence)

Use your own transaction signatures against your own RPC as the ground truth for 'landed'. Bundle-ID endpoints have short retention (five minutes in flight, recent slots for statuses) and DBI bundles are outside them; keep bundle-status polling for diagnosis only (in-flight state, drop reason). The jito-bundle crate likewise polls both the Jito API and Solana RPC. (medium confidence)

Maker Priority (MPP) and Preconfirmations are not general landing routes. MPP: enrolled market makers send pre-signed price updates to a separate UDP endpoint (PTPU) on each BAM Node; they are scheduled first in every auction batch, need no tip, but must pay at least 1 lamport per compute unit; Jito manages enrollment. Preconfirmations: a read-only stream of transactions a BAM leader has committed to executing, sold through Helius and Triton, with a p50 advantage of 5-10 ms over shred feeds in early tests; they are not finality and exist only for BAM leaders. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

A Jito bundle is a list of up to 5 fully signed transactions that execute sequentially, within a single slot, and atomically: if any transaction fails, none are committed. Bundles cannot cross slot boundaries. (high confidence)

Transactions are submitted to the Block Engine (JSON-RPC POST /api/v1/bundles, method sendBundle, or gRPC) as base64 strings (recommended); base58 is slow and marked DEPRECATED in Jito's docs. Maximum 5 transactions per request. (high confidence)

Jito's default send rate limit is 1 request per second per IP per region, with no auth key needed for default sends; exceeding it returns a 429 or rate-limit error; higher limits need a ticket. Spreading sends across regional Block Engine endpoints (mainnet global plus Amsterdam, Dublin, Frankfurt and others) therefore multiplies capacity. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

A Jito bundle is a list of up to 5 fully signed transactions that the Block Engine passes to a Jito-Solana leader to execute sequentially and atomically within one slot. A bundle cannot cross a slot boundary, and if any transaction fails none of the transactions are committed. (high confidence)

The Block Engine runs parallel auctions. Bundles whose account-lock patterns intersect on a writable account ((w,w), (r,w) or (w,r)) compete in one auction; bundles that do not intersect, or that overlap only on reads, run in separate auctions. Within an auction bundles are ranked by requested tip per requested compute unit, and Jito submits the highest-paying combination to the validator up to a compute-unit limit. (high confidence)

Jito's JSON-RPC defaults to base58 transaction encoding, but base58 is deprecated and slow. Send base64 and set the encoding option to base64 explicitly on every sendBundle and sendTransaction call. (high confidence)

When a Block Engine rate limit is exceeded the response is HTTP 429 or a rate-limit error that names the limit hit, and Jito says default sends no longer need an approved auth key. The jito-bundle Rust crate treats 429s, timeouts and on-chain failures as separate cases in its status handling. (medium confidence)

Jito's documented default limit is 1 request per second per IP per region; a higher limit needs a support ticket. This number comes from one source, Jito's docs, and no second source confirms it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Wrapping a sandwich-prone transaction in your own bundle keeps an attacker from including it in a sandwich bundle, because bundles cannot be nested on Jito. Jupiter's MEV-protection setting works this way by issuing a length-one bundle. The IMC authors caution that this does not stop all front-running, and Solana's guide adds that tight slippage is the most effective single defense. (medium confidence)

Never put a Jito tip account in an address lookup table. Jito warns that tips must not use lookup tables, the jito-bundle crate validates this up front because a lookup table that contains a tip account makes the transaction fail at runtime, and Solana's dontfront guide repeats the rule (the dontfront account itself may be loaded through a table). (high confidence)

Alternatives to Jito submission trade away atomicity or coverage. Gerus Lab (a vendor blog) says QuickNode's Lil-JIT cannot guarantee atomic multi-transaction execution, and that Astralane's private relay has smaller validator coverage than Jito and an extra relay hop. RPC Fast says some of Jito's tip share moved to Astralane and Lil-JIT in Q1 2026. Neither source publishes measurements. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-07)

A Jito bundle is up to five fully signed transactions that run in the listed order, atomically and all-or-nothing, inside one slot (a bundle cannot cross a slot boundary). Only a leader running Jito-Solana or BAM can process it; Jito's docs say tips do nothing on leaders that are not Jito-Solana. (high confidence)

Block Engine sendBundle (JSON-RPC POST /api/v1/bundles) takes up to five fully signed transactions and returns a bundle_id, the SHA-256 hash of the transaction signatures, on acceptance only. The encoding option defaults to base58 (slow, deprecated), so pass {'encoding': 'base64'} explicitly when sending base64 strings. sendTransaction on /api/v1/transactions proxies to the validator, always sets skip_preflight=true, and with ?bundleOnly=true goes out only as a one-transaction bundle for revert protection; the bundle ID then arrives in the x-bundle-id response header. (high confidence)

DBI error and limit behaviour: HTTP 401 means no valid UUID in x-jito-auth; HTTP 429 means the per-key limit was exceeded (applied separately at each BAM node; QUIC drops excess packets instead; the numeric limit is set when the key is issued and not published); QUIC application close code 2 means the keypair is not allowlisted or not yet active, or connections from one IP arrive too fast, so reconnect with backoff, not in a tight loop. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)

The Block Engine's bundle result protocol separates outcomes: Accepted (forwarded to a validator, possibly several), and Rejected with one of StateAuctionBidRejected (bid too low for its state auction), WinningBatchBidRejected (won its state auction but lost against other winners), SimulationFailure (names the offending tx signature), InternalError, or DroppedBundle. Block engines simulate bundles and pick the most profitable combinations. (medium confidence)

Put the tip instruction in the same transaction as the strategy logic, with post-transaction checks, so a failed strategy does not pay the tip. If space is tight, put state assertions (slot, balance) in the tip transaction. A standalone tip transaction inside a bundle increases exposure to 'uncle bandit' rebroadcast of individual bundle transactions. (medium confidence)

Atomicity does not hold if a block is uncled: bundle transactions can be rebroadcast individually outside the bundle ('unbundling'). Jito says Jito itself never leaks bundles, but during uncled-block situations users are exposed. Mitigation is pre/post account checks inside the transactions so a lone rebroadcast tx is harmless. (medium confidence)

Tips only influence a leader that runs Jito-Solana. Jito warns that tips do not prioritize transactions at validators that are not Jito-Solana leaders, so tipping then is wasted. Bundle inclusion is therefore tied to the slots where a Jito-enabled validator produces blocks. (high confidence)

Jito publishes regional Block Engine URLs of the form https://<region>.mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf (amsterdam, dublin, frankfurt, london, ny, slc, singapore, tokyo) plus a global geo-routed https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf. Helius forwards bundles to the global endpoint and lets callers pick a region with the jito-region header (ams, dub, fra, lon, nyc, slc, sgp, tyo, mainnet). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Jito lists JSON-RPC SDKs for Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust and Go that wrap send_bundle, get_bundle_statuses, get_inflight_bundle_statuses, get_tip_accounts and send_transaction. Community code uses jito-ts for the gRPC SearcherClient. The third-party jito-bundle Rust crate adds tip strategies, pre-send checks (bundle size, lookup-table safety, transaction size) and confirmation polling across both the Jito API and Solana RPC. (medium confidence)

Before Alpenglow activation Jito planned to put all mainnet BAM nodes into Maintenance Mode. Connected validators revert to the ordinary Jito-Agave Block Engine mode and keep accepting bundles through it, while the Maker Priority Plugin (MPP) and DBI are unavailable. DBI users are told to use the legacy Block Engine bundle path, and standard bundle senders have no action. BAM nodes return gradually after activation, with timing announced on Jito's Discord, so the post-activation state is not confirmed in the sources read. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13)

Put the tip instruction inside the same transaction as the strategy logic, with post-state assertions, so a failing strategy never pays the tip. If transaction space forces a separate tip transaction, add assertions to it (slot check, balance check) so the tip is conditional. Jito warns that standalone tip transactions inside bundles increase exposure to uncle-bandit scenarios. (high confidence)

jitodontfront: add any valid pubkey starting with jitodontfront as a read-only account to any instruction. The Block Engine then rejects any bundle containing that transaction unless it is at index 0. Several such transactions are allowed only if they are contiguous at the front and each shares a signer with the first. It works with sendTransaction, sendBundle and address lookup tables, runs on mainnet and testnet only, and the account need not exist on chain. Jito says it may reduce sandwich attacks but does not guarantee protection, and it applies only inside the Block Engine. (high confidence)

DBI bundles do not appear in the Jito bundle explorer or its API, and DBI bundle IDs do not match Block Engine records. A JSON-RPC bundle ID means only that the node queued the request; a QUIC acknowledgment means only that the stream was accepted. Confirm landing with getSignatureStatuses on your own RPC using the transaction signatures. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)

Helius Sender (a Helius-run path across Helius, Jito, Harmonic and other routes) has stricter submission rules than the Jito Block Engine: a single transaction must carry both a tip transfer to a designated tip account and a compute-unit-price instruction or it is rejected, and sendBundle takes at most four transactions with at least one carrying the tip. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
